clue.text: Money needed to get in at international game

indicators.note: the money is said to let the other pieces get in, so they sit inside it

parts.note: pence is small British money
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone needs cash to be admitted to an international match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' is not a sport here but the card game for one player.
explanation.definitionFit: The solitary card game played with one deck is called this in Britain; Americans say solitaire.

clue.text: Entering factory, I moan

indicators.note: the letter I goes into the factory word

parts.note: a plant is an industrial works

explanation.surface: Going into the works, someone complains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entering' puts I inside PLANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A lament or complaint, a literary word for a grievance.

clue.text: Puzzled about food being dispatched in the main

parts.note: thrown means confused or puzzled
over means about, concerning
board is food, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: Confused about the food being served at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is the sea (old poetic sense), so being dispatched in it means tossed off a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurled off a ship into the sea, the main being an old word for ocean.

clue.text: Delving into Exodus (second part of Pentateuch), high priest reveals knowledge

indicators.note: the rearranged priest digs inside the other letters

parts.note: Ex is the abbreviation of the book Exodus

indicators.note: the second letter of the word Pentateuch is taken
high means drunk, so the letters of priest reel into a new order

explanation.surface: A high priest studying Exodus, second book of the Pentateuch, shows his learning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second part of' gives E, and 'high' (drunk) rearranges the priest; 'Delving into' puts those letters inside EX + E. The high priest of the surface is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Skill or specialist know-how in a field.

clue.text: College right to accept orphan girl is more astute

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the girl goes inside

parts.note: Annie is the orphan of the comic strip and musical

explanation.surface: A college is right to take in an orphan who is sharper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accept' puts ANNIE inside C and R. Little Orphan Annie is the comic-strip orphan.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewder, the comparative of canny, a Scottish word for shrewd.

clue.text: Batman liberated little bird

indicators.note: letters set free from their order can regroup, so the word Batman is rearranged

explanation.surface: The caped crusader sets a small bird free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liberated' rearranges BATMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A bantam is a small breed of domestic fowl.

clue.text: Sole I found attached to a line

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A fish found tied to a fishing line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sole' suggests the fish; it means only. 'found attached to' joins ONE onto A L.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitary, without company, like the only one.

clue.text: Book getting you a bit down?

definitions.meaning: a novel by A E W Mason about cowardice and redemption
a few plumes are a small amount of soft feather down

explanation.walkthrough: Down here is fluffy feathering, not sadness; four plumes are a little bit of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mason adventure novel; also, literally, a handful of plumes, a small amount of fluff.

clue.text: Observes cars crossing province

indicators.note: the cars word spans the province, so the province sits inside

parts.note: motors are cars
NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province

explanation.surface: Someone watches cars driving across a province.
explanation.walkthrough: Northern Ireland is known in Britain as the Province, abbreviated NI.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep watch on or check over time.

clue.text: Cries of delight from doctor before surgical procedures

indicators.note: the doctor piece is placed before the operations

parts.note: Doctor Who is the TV time traveller, so doctor gives who
ops are operations

explanation.surface: Patients shout with joy at seeing the doctor before their operations.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor Who is the long-running BBC science-fiction series, so 'doctor' gives WHO; 'before' sets the order.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud shouts of excitement or joy.

clue.text: Result of being 2 is of little significance

definitions.meaning: 2 refers to 2-down: someone thrown off a ship ends up as a small splash in the sea
an idiom for an amount too small to matter

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition reads the idiom literally: a person tossed into the sea becomes a tiny speck in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A literal speck of water in the sea, and the idiom for a negligible contribution.

clue.text: Fresher offered pot at end of induction

indicators.note: only the closing letter of the word induction is wanted

parts.note: a ewer is a large jug or pot

explanation.surface: A new student is given a pot at the close of freshers' week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresher' looks like a noun for a new student but is the comparative adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Something more recent is less stale, the comparative of new.

clue.text: Nasty odour in centre of Exeter is sorted

indicators.note: something nasty is twisted out of shape, so these letters are rearranged
the two middle letters of the six-letter word Exeter are taken

explanation.surface: An unpleasant smell in the middle of Exeter has been dealt with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' takes ET from EXETER; 'Nasty' rearranges ODOUR, IN and ET. Exeter is a city in Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: Problems that are resolved or settled are smoothed away like creases.

clue.text: Office item, one installed by manager

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, as if fitted in

parts.note: a coper is one who copes, who manages
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A manager has put one piece of equipment into the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'installed by' puts I inside COPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A photocopying machine is standard office equipment.

clue.text: I'll search high and low for a domestic cleaner

definitions.meaning: one who scours, searching thoroughly everywhere
a pad for scrubbing pans in the kitchen

explanation.surface: Someone vows to hunt everywhere for a cleaning lady.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a charwoman, but the cleaner is a kitchen pad.
explanation.definitionFit: To scour is both to search thoroughly and to scrub, so one who searches and a scrubbing pad.

clue.text: Take charge of old chemical company, with calamitous result all round

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the result surrounds the company, so the company goes inside

parts.note: fate can mean death or ruin
ICI was Imperial Chemical Industries, a now-defunct British firm

explanation.surface: Running an old chemical firm ended in disaster all round.
explanation.walkthrough: ICI (Imperial Chemical Industries) was a large British chemical company; 'all round' says the calamitous result surrounds it. 'of' reads as part of the definition but supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To preside or act as the person in authority, as a referee or priest does.

clue.text: Musician is appearing in bar a bit later

indicators.note: the bit comes later than the bar

parts.note: to bar is to ban

indicators.note: the word is shows up inside the other letters

parts.note: a jot is a tiny bit

explanation.surface: A performer turns up at a bar a little late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' looks like a link verb but goes inside the bit, and 'later' places the bit after the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of the plucked, round-bodied stringed instrument.

clue.text: See gals warring, never getting on

indicators.note: fighting implies disorder, so the letters of see gals are rearranged

explanation.surface: Watch girls fighting who never get along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'warring' rearranges SEE GALS. 'getting on' means growing old, not getting along.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who never seems to grow older is timeless.

clue.text: Naughty ones taken outside room for telling off

indicators.note: the rearranged ones go around the room
naughty suggests unruly, so the letters of ones are rearranged

explanation.surface: Naughty children are taken out of the room to be scolded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naughty' rearranges the ones to SEON, and 'taken outside' wraps that around the room.
explanation.definitionFit: A long moralising lecture or reprimand, by extension from a preacher's address.

clue.text: Sacked by supervisor in the end, I did a runner

indicators.note: only the closing letter of the word supervisor is wanted

parts.note: British slang for running away, fled

explanation.surface: Fired by my boss at last, I ran off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sacked' suggests fired from a job; here it means plundered.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack is to search through and steal, as a burglar does with drawers.

clue.text: Book kept for posterity, with covers removed

indicators.note: a book's covers are its outsides, so first and last letters go

parts.note: preserved means kept for future generations

explanation.surface: A book saved for future readers has lost its covers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with covers removed' drops the first and last letters of PRESERVED.
explanation.definitionFit: To book is to arrange in advance, to secure a place.

clue.text: Knowledge American briefly acquired of African country

parts.note: ken is knowledge, as in beyond my ken

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a Yank is an American

explanation.surface: An American briefly gained knowledge about an African nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts the final K from YANK.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective for things from the East African nation whose capital is Nairobi.

clue.text: Judge outdated careers as limited opportunities for workers

parts.note: obs is the dictionary abbreviation for obsolete
to career is to rush along, as hares do

explanation.surface: A judge dismisses old-fashioned professions as offering few openings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'careers' looks like a noun but is the verb meaning to rush.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrangements where two people split one post, giving each part-time work.

clue.text: Work secured by female, one with aspirations

indicators.note: the work is held fast inside the female word

parts.note: her is a female pronoun
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A woman lands a job and has high hopes.
explanation.walkthrough: Op is short for opus, a musical work, not a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who wishes or expects things will turn out well.

clue.text: Piece of meat that is put on dish

parts.note: a cut is a piece of meat from the butcher
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A slice of meat is served on a plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dish' looks like a plate; it means an attractive person.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a good-looking person; both words mean someone attractive.

clue.text: I purloin pounds state's invested unwisely?

indicators.note: to invest is literally to clothe, so the state wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: NY is New York state
to appropriate is to take for oneself, steal
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to stealing money that the government has put into poor ventures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested' suggests money but means clothed: the state wraps round the stolen pounds. The question mark flags the wry definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in an unsuitable or ill-judged way.

clue.text: Members of royal family wanting duke to participate in foreign tours

indicators.note: the duke takes part by joining inside the other letters
foreign suggests strange, so the letters of tours are rearranged

explanation.surface: Royals who don't want a duke on their overseas trips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' rearranges TOURS to TUORS, and 'to participate in' puts D inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The English royal dynasty from Henry VII to Elizabeth I.

clue.text: Jazz pianist, someone drowning English tenor

indicators.note: something drowned is submerged within, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: a person is someone

explanation.surface: A jazz pianist and someone else drowning an English singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drowning' puts E and T inside PERSON. Oscar Peterson was a Canadian jazz pianist.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar of that surname was a celebrated Canadian jazz pianist.
